findings.title: Escaped or unbalanced quote swallows every later pipe, so trailing filters silently stop being split off

serves.scenario: The scanner has no escape handling and no recovery for an unterminated quote. In `x ?? "a\"b" | trim` the backslash-escaped quote closes the quote, the real closing quote reopens it, and the ` | trim` pipe, which is outside the quoted default, is treated as quoted text. The same happens with a stray apostrophe before a pipe (`x ?? "abc | trim`, or any lone ' or " earlier in the expression). At base these pipes separated filters; at head they do not, so the filter is dropped and the core handed to the ?? parsing becomes the whole string. Whether that surfaces as wrong output or a different error depends on the unshown remainder of parseVariableExpression, which is why this is a risk and not a confirmed defect.

findings.rubric: A default with an escaped or unbalanced quote does not hang or throw a new error type. Also the goal-critical question: does a pipe outside quotes still separate filters, including after a quoted default?
findings.reproduction: Call splitOutsideQuotes on `x ?? "a\"b" | trim` with separator `|`: head returns 1 part (the whole string); base expr.split('|') returned 2 parts (`x ?? "a\"b" `, ` trim`). Then render `${{x ?? "a\"b" | trim}}` and `${{x ?? "abc | trim}}` with x missing at base and at head and compare output and error class; any difference confirms the regression. Smallest fix: inside a quote, skip the character after a backslash; and if the scan ends with a quote still open, fall back to the previous split for the unterminated tail (or only open a quote when a matching closer exists later in the text). The loop is a single linear pass, so there is no hang in either case.

findings.title: A quoted default that holds both an escaped quote and a pipe still splits at the pipe (unchanged from base)

serves.scenario: `${{x ?? "a\"|b"}}` with x missing: the backslash-escaped quote closes the quoted run, the pipe splits, and `b"` is treated as a filter name, so the default does not render whole. Base behaved the same way, so this is not a regression or a new error type, and the spec does not define escapes; noted for the lead only.

findings.reproduction: Call splitOutsideQuotes on `x ?? "a\"|b"` with separator `|`: it returns 2 parts (`x ?? "a\"` and `b"`), the same as base `expr.split('|')`. Rendering with x missing should give the same Unknown filter error at base and at head.
